subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stopped counting days and started counting how much his boots hurt.
source_quote: We'd been on the road south out of the Silver Marches long enough that I'd stopped counting days and started counting how much my boots hurt.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the silence in Daggerford wasn't natural.
source_quote: The hill giants I grew up with — they had a word for a silence that wasn't natural.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin watched a woman cross the road to avoid a conversation and then pretend she hadn't.
source_quote: I watched a woman cross the road to avoid a conversation and then pretend she hadn't.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stared at the bronze forearm monument longer than he should have.
source_quote: I stared at it for longer than I should have.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to make sure he hadn't misread the Dwarven inscription.
source_quote: I read it twice because Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought about how many towns north of Daggerford had similar stories but hadn't put up monuments.
source_quote: I stood in the doorway of the River Shining and thought about how many towns north of here had a story like this, and just hadn't put up a bronze arm about it yet.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the unnatural silence in Daggerford.
source_quote: Grygum noticed it too, I could tell, though he didn't say anything.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum made a noise when he read that Tarvis Ulain had served Bahamut.
source_quote: Grygum made a sound when he got to the part confirming Tarvis had served Bahamut — not a word, just the noise a person makes when something clicks into place.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was quiet in a way that meant he was adding something to the list.
source_quote: Grygum was quiet. Not the usual quiet. The kind where he's adding something to the list.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the Stroudite inscription on the monument was either ignored or tolerated.
source_quote: The priest conceded, looking left, looking right, like the Stroudites might be listening.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was convinced the silence in Elin was not absence but insistence.
source_quote: Silence isn't absence. Seven years old and drawing the same thing on every flat surface is not nothing — it's insistence.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the madness from the Underdark was reaching the surface through Elin.
source_quote: Oh," I said, as something slid into place. "There's all the people — hearing voices?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum still thinks about Zuggtmoy and probably will for the rest of his life.
source_quote: I still think about Zuggtmoy, and will probably continue thinking about Zuggtmoy for the rest of my life.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum wrote down Elin’s words: 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: I wrote it down. It is what I do.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Elin’s condition was interior and untouchable by conventional means.
source_quote: Whatever was happening inside Elin was interior in a way that made it untouchable through conventional means.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suspected a tenuous connection between Elin’s condition and Daz’s headache.
source_quote: There's some kind of tenuous connection there?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum filed the phenomenon under open questions and kept writing.
source_quote: I filed it under open questions and kept writing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to wear armor.
source_quote: Daz refused, saying armor would only slow him down

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the pressure in his own head.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz found Whistler’s restraint in taking only what was needed from Tiamat’s hoard genuinely impressive.
source_quote: I found that, I mean, genuinely impressive. The restraint of it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted the exits in the Burning Wizard Inn.
source_quote: I noted the exits. Front door, obvious. Side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels. Stairs to the upper rooms. The window behind the performer's corner, narrow but workable in an emergency.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed the wall in the Burning Wizard Inn remembers the wizard’s death.
source_quote: My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires.
source_quote: Grygum leaned forward — he has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is Bahamutian, with sentimentality for Stroud.
source_quote: he explained that he was Bahamutian, with sentimentality for the other.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum received the love song about Stroud's chess game in the way he receives most things downgraded by translation: politely, and with the file already updated.
source_quote: Grygum received this in the way he receives most things downgraded by translation: politely, and with the file already updated.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that the only love he remembers during the previous campaign involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.
source_quote: The only love I remember during the previous campaign," he said, "involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes things have to be done with a grain of salt.
source_quote: These things have to be done with a grain of salt.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noticed a young human scholar in the far corner reciting something under his breath — a rhythmic, almost liturgical chant.
source_quote: There was a young human scholar in the far corner — not a human scholar, a *young* human scholar, because those are meaningfully different things and I did not want to get the category wrong — who was reciting something under his breath. A chant of some kind. Rhythmic, almost liturgical.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noticed the scholar's breathing was almost right but wrong by a hair in a way that required knowledge of the correct version to notice.
source_quote: His breathing was almost right. The pauses fell almost correctly. The pattern was almost the one it was supposed to be — and wrong by a hair in a way that took actual knowledge of the correct version to notice.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator knows the chant well enough to know what the scholar was doing wrong.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong,

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator realized the specific wrongness in the chant was not a beginner's error but a very particular kind of degradation.
source_quote: the specific wrongness of it — the way he syncopated his breath against the syllables, or tried to — was not a beginner's error. It was a very particular kind of degradation.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator has seen this pattern of degradation before — twice — in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher.
source_quote: I have seen it before. Twice. Eldred had it, earlier in the journey — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator wrote down the exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, and the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin found the sight of Dawnbringer lighting up the sea peaceful rather than counterproductive.
source_quote: Thorin apparently found this peaceful rather than counterproductive, which I note without judgment.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin came back in with the settled look of a man who had had a thought that satisfied him.
source_quote: He came back in with the settled look of a man who had had a thought that satisfied him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes life takes you in weird directions and weird places, and you just gotta go with it.
source_quote: Life takes you in weird directions and weird places," he said. "You just gotta go with it.

subject: Thorin's belief
fact: The narrator has not yet decided whether Thorin's statement is wisdom or resignation, and suspects there may not be much difference.
source_quote: I have been thinking about that sentence since he said it. I have not yet decided whether it is wisdom or resignation. Possibly there is not much difference.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir came back down from the roof settled, with the expression of someone closing an internal argument, not opening an external one.
source_quote: Zalthir climbed to the roof to meditate. He came back down later, settled. The expression of someone closing an internal argument, not opening an external one.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said 'Hmm, true,' in the tone of a man completing an internal argument rather than beginning an external one.
source_quote: He said "Hmm, true," about something, in the tone of a man completing an internal argument rather than beginning an external one.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator understands that the wall remembers better than he would like to.
source_quote: I find I understand that better than I would like to.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz went quiet beside the narrator somewhere around the second hour of walking — not his usual quiet.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz put his hand to his temple and kept it there.
source_quote: His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Daz's unusual quiet and hand-to-temple gesture but did not say anything yet.
source_quote: I noticed. I didn't say anything yet.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed Daz's change and asked whether it connected to the spreading madness from the Underdark.
source_quote: Grygum noticed too, and asked whether it connected to the voices — the spreading madness we'd watched move through the Underdark like groundwater through stone.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes something is wrong and tenuous with Daz's condition.
source_quote: He couldn't pin it down, he said. Something wrong, something tenuous.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm noticed the bag containing Glabbagool and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy and found it unacceptable.
source_quote: She'd noticed the bag. Specifically, she'd noticed what was in the bag — because when we'd come through the gate, we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him, which she apparently found unacceptable,

subject: Spy
fact: The spy is furious about being treated as a guest rather than a prisoner.
source_quote: The spy, for her part, was furious.

subject: Spy
fact: The spy announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.
source_quote: She turned to Kalan and announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was glad to be asked about the spy's status.
source_quote: Glabbagool was glad to be asked.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool found the spy entertaining because she kept trying to kill him, and they had become great friends.
source_quote: He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream. He'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation. She'd scream about the meditation. Then they'd talk. He said they'd become great friends.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is ambivalent about watching the spy.
source_quote: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool paused and asked Zalthir directly: 'Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?'
source_quote: Glabbagool paused, and asked me directly: "Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?"

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool took Zalthir's affirmation seriously and believed the work counted.
source_quote: Glabbagool took this with complete seriousness. The work counted; he had been told so.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool committed to keeping an eye on the spy.
source_quote: I will keep an eye on her!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the note on Khell-Vire's desk: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.'
source_quote: On Khell-Vire's desk, visible from where I was standing: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Zalthir stared at it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had played this game before — the shadow monk pedagogy — and found it annoying.
source_quote: I've played this game before, my friends," Zalthir said, which was directed at no one in particular, or possibly at us, or possibly at the entire tradition of shadow monk pedagogy stretching back five centuries.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir responded flatly to Khell-Vire's question: 'Granted, given that constraint or specification, can you clarify?'
source_quote: Zalthir's response was immediate and flat: "Granted, given that constraint or specification, can you clarify?"

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was annoyed by Khell-Vire's line of questioning, in the way he found shadow monk classes annoying.
source_quote: Zalthir, to his credit, didn't pretend to find it profound. He found it annoying, in the specific way that all those shadow monk classes he'd ignored had been annoying, which told its own story.

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk said Zalthir skipped the third breath, didn't enter his ki in the hara, and let it bleed into his fingertips like a poison.
source_quote: You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll.

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk said to Zalthir: 'Show me what else you haven't learned.'
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk.
source_quote: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk.

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk said to Zalthir: 'You have learned nothing.' after Zalthir failed the Weightless Shadow.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk asked Zalthir: 'Did you not practice your forms while traveling?'
source_quote: Did you not practice your forms while traveling?

subject: The monk
fact: The monk was, by every available indication, genuinely impressed.
source_quote: He was, by every available indication, genuinely impressed.

subject: The monk
fact: The monk stood there for a moment, something recalibrating behind his blindness.
source_quote: He stood there for a moment, something recalibrating behind his blindness

subject: The monk
fact: The monk thought perhaps he'd been approaching this the wrong way.
source_quote: Perhaps I've been approaching this the wrong way.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir found the manual aggravating and ignored it.
source_quote: Zalthir found the manual aggravating, ignored it, and built something better.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed he had built something better than the manual.
source_quote: He was now being told that the thing he'd built was the most interesting thing about him.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a moment from the Underdark where he'd found a way to punch through the shadows themselves.
source_quote: Zalthir recalled something from the Underdark — a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir acknowledged that the shadow monks had driven him nuts.
source_quote: Yeah, definitely.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin referred to the drow as 'Pocket Drow.'
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was satisfied that the gelatinous cube had not been dismissed as a mindless digestive system.
source_quote: I noted with some satisfaction that we had not brought a gelatinous cube this far — through the Underdark, through Waterdeep, into the libraries of Candlekeep — to have him dismissed as a mindless digestive system before lunch.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thought the appointment was technically his idea, but it was really Thorin's.
source_quote: The appointment was Daz's idea, technically, which meant it was my idea that Daz had first.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz didn't know what pronoun to use for Dawnbringer.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but, you know, whether it's them? Is it her? He, her?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt relieved when Philemon acknowledged Dawnbringer as a friend.
source_quote: That landed somewhere I hadn't expected. I hadn't been told to be relieved by that. I was anyway.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood the impulse behind making a joke about the rebound relationship.
source_quote: I understood the impulse behind the joke.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed Dawnbringer needed to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed Dawnbringer needed to grieve.
source_quote: And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thought the months in the Underdark had cost Dawnbringer deeply.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun. What that had cost her — I knew some of it, and I probably didn't know most of it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz hoped Dawnbringer would grow a plus one.
source_quote: Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed his headache had been bothering him since arriving at Candlekeep.
source_quote: My head had been complaining since we arrived at Candlekeep.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the headache was not from the sun but from the proximity to knowledge.
source_quote: The proximity — to the knowledge, or to whatever sat underneath the knowledge — was producing a friction I had been mis-attributing to the sun all day.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz did not know who he was or his history.
source_quote: I don't know who I am, or my history

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knew he couldn't afford the usual deceptive approach because he didn't know what he was hiding.
source_quote: When you don't know what you're hiding, you can't protect it. Better to lay everything out and watch what someone else picks up.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood the grammar of Menzoberranzan's politics, even if he couldn't recall the facts.
source_quote: I knew most of this. Not as facts retrieved from memory, but as grammar.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the word 'blithering idiot' didn't fit him.
source_quote: I asked the second logical question. 'Am I the blithering idiot?'

subject: Daz's origins
fact: Daz does not know why his head hurts or who he was before being imprisoned.
source_quote: I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Daz's past
fact: Daz's memory of his life before imprisonment is missing.
source_quote: I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt a recognition when reading the term 'Daz'issin' and its lit. meaning 'small shadow,' as if it resonated with his own name.
source_quote: I gotta tell you, the first line of this, where it says, *Daz'issin*, and lit., *small shadow*, made me feel like I was reading, like, millennial shorthand. And that I didn't understand it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suspects his name may be a shortened form of 'Daz'issin,' a maternal diminutive used for boys mothers hoped would live.
source_quote: Well, isn't my name, Daz? Maybe it's my full name?

subject: Daz'issin
fact: The full identity and history of Daz'issin is missing, as the appendix referenced by the footnote was deliberately removed with a razor.
source_quote: I found a footnote instead... The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne's body stopped matching her words, revealing a careful navigation of information beyond the public record.
source_quote: Yvenne's body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne maintains the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say.
source_quote: the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne refused to answer whether Daz's name is connected to Daz'issin, leaving the question unresolved.
source_quote: She said nothing.

subject: Daz's origin
fact: The possibility that Daz's name is a maternal diminutive from a lost house remains unverified and unspoken.
source_quote: She told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized silence from Yvenne is an answer in the ledger — an acknowledgment of hidden truth.
source_quote: She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz carries the unspoken weight of being possibly named by a mother who used a dying lineage's term to protect him.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the ritual archive privileges of the fourth seat in Menzoberranzan and connected them to the concept of 'struck' as institutional erasure.
source_quote: She mentioned, almost as an aside, that the fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records.
